applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No bilateral investment treaty in Bermuda's own capacity; Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory without separate treaty-making competence. The OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters has been extended to Bermuda (effective 1 August 2014).
UK-negotiated Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with the United States (1988) and other G20/OECD states are in force; TIEAs do not establish investment protection.
Potential future UK investment protection commitments may extend to Bermuda on an ad hoc basis; no active UK-Bermuda bilateral investment treaty (BIT) exists.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime Act 1997; Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2008 (as amended); Beneficial Ownership (Disclosure and Use) Act 2017 and Beneficial Ownership (Disclosure and Use) Regulations 2017; Bermuda Monetary Authority AML/CFT Code of Practice 2008 (as revised)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / licensed notary public in the UK or jurisdiction of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory interactive screening against UN consolidated list, UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI), EU consolidated list, and US OFAC SDN list; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, family members, and close associates; continuous monitoring triggered by transaction or material event; risk tier maintained as low for PropTech SaaS but with independent verification of corporate shareholders' ultimate ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (Department of Corporate Services, Registry General); company name clearance and incorporation filings must be submitted through a licensed corporate services provider; public name search is available via the official Bermuda Government corporate registry portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin/English script; any non-English name must be accompanied by a romanized transliteration and English translation; the Registrar has discretion to require a name that is not misleading and does not conflict with established trademarks
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: International Business (unless entity is an exempted enterprise under qualifying regimes)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies within 14 business days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds for distinctiveness and compliance with the Companies Act 1981; if the Registrar refuses the reconsideration, the applicant may appeal to the Supreme Court of Bermuda within 21 days of the refusal under section 10 of the Companies Act 1981; a new name application may be concurrently filed to prevent delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted. A physical registered address in Bermuda is mandatory, and it must be maintained at the office of a licensed corporate service provider or a physically verifiable Bermudian address; incidental virtual mailbox-only services do not satisfy the statutory requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 12–18% unannounced inspection probability in the first 12 months for a low-risk, revenue-generation PropTech SaaS with no licensed activity; inspections are performed by the BMA under the AML/CFT framework or by the Registrar of Companies for substance compliance; risk mitigators include clear physical presence and genuine economic substance documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1981 (Bermuda), as amended; constitutional and exempted-company provisions under ss. 4-6 (incorporation and exempted company), s. 14 (certificate of incorporation), s. 51 (registered office), ss. 52-53 (directors and secretary), and the Economic Substance Amendment Act 2018 for annual substance registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda (online e-Registry portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws, together with the Statutory Declaration of Compliance and Notice of Registered Office, filed under the Companies Act 1981
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit requirement; the Memorandum must declare authorized capital (default BMD/USD 12,000; higher tiers attract higher fees); at least one ordinary share must be issued and fully paid to the subscriber, and further shares may be allotted by board resolution against SaaS development and working-capital contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the allotment and issue of the initial subscribed ordinary shares to the subscribers be and the same is hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at the address in Bermuda set forth in the Notice of Registered Office and that [Name] be and is hereby appointed resident representative. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the persons listed in the schedule be and are hereby appointed as directors and corporate secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all pre-incorporation actions of the subscribers, including adoption of the Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws and payment of fees, be and the same are hereby ratified. DATED this day of , 2025.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda (e-Registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability application through the e-Registry portal. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name and must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd.', or another approved suffix. Upon acceptance, the name is reserved for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Name availability request form
Statement of proposed principal activity (ISIC 6201 PropTech SaaS platform)
Proposed company name ending in 'Limited'
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on similarity grounds, file an alternate reserved name immediately; a written appeal may be lodged with the Registrar within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Bermuda corporate service provider / registered agent acting as preparer before the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A Bermuda-licensed resident agent prepares the Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws. The subscriber shareholders execute the documents before a notary public, and each proposed director, secretary, and resident representative signs a consent-to-act form.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum of Association (name, capital, registered-office and objects clauses)
Bye-Laws adopted by subscribers
Consent-to-Act forms of each director and the corporate secretary
Consent of resident representative and registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any notarization defects or capital-clause drafting issues and re-execute the affected pages; minor amendments may be completed by supplemental instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application and statutory fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies — e-Registry online filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation package electronically: statutory declaration of compliance, executed memorandum, bye-laws, consents, and notice of registered office. Pay the tier-based incorporation fee of USD/BMD 1,780 for authorized capital not exceeding BMD 12,000; the filing fee is remitted by wire or card through the registry portal.
required_dossiers: Statutory Declaration of Compliance under s. 4 of the Companies Act 1981
Executed Memorandum of Association
Bye-Laws
Consent-to-Act of directors, secretary, and resident representative
Notice of Registered Office
Government fee remittance reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency query, respond with corrected documents or written explanation within 14 calendar days; ministerial corrections are resubmitted without an additional full incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and establishment of statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar registers the company, allocates a unique registration number, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation under s. 14. The corporate service provider obtains certified copies and opens the statutory registers of members, directors, charges, and beneficial owners at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (original)
Certified extracts of the Memorandum and Bye-Laws
Registration number allocation record
Statutory register index and beneficial ownership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For typographical errors in the certificate, file a corrective cover letter supported by constitutional documents; the Registry re-issues an amended certificate within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation governance: first board meeting and share issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company directors and resident representative acting at the Bermuda registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to ratify the share allotment, approve the registered office and resident representative appointments, and appoint officers. Issue share certificates and record entries in the register of members; execute the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution contained in this dossier and place the signed minutes in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Pro-Forma First Board Resolution (signed and dated)
Minutes of the first board meeting
Share certificates and register of members
Officer and resident representative consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment is invalid under the Bye-Laws, pass a corrective board resolution at a subsequent meeting and re-file executed consents with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Economic substance registration and annual compliance activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies (Economic Substance Division / ESA filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the exempted company under the Economic Substance Amendment Act 2018 and complete the annual entity-type and relevant-activity declaration. A pure ISIC 6201 PropTech SaaS platform is normally classified as a non-core relevant entity; maintain documentation showing that all substantive business activity is conducted outside Bermuda, and confirm the annual exempted-company government fee and beneficial ownership filing obligations.
required_dossiers: Economic substance registration confirmation
Beneficial ownership declaration and register
Annual exempted-company fee remittance
Exemption certificate application under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act (if applying for tax-exemption comfort)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies a relevant-activity classification, file a corrected annual economic substance return with supporting evidence of management, employees, and physical premises; voluntary disclosure mitigates penalty exposure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable — no physical industrial establishment exists for the ISIC 6201 PropTech SaaS platform; purely cloud-based operations require no Bermuda industrial or manufacturing license. The Department of ICT Policy and Innovation (Cabinet Office, Bermuda) has informational oversight for digital-services policy only.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — exempted company status together with the annual government fee satisfies operational authorization; no separate operating or manufacturing permit is issued for software-as-a-service delivery.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Bermuda Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical construction, land disturbance, or industrial discharge; full EIA not required for a cloud-hosted PropTech software platform.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or process-emission thresholds apply. The Company must comply with the Bermuda Personal Information Protection Act 2016 for data handling and DENR waste regulations for disposal of electronic equipment; production servers are hosted in ISO-27001 certified data centers outside Bermuda, generating no local physical emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — the Bermuda registered office is a virtual administrative address with no fire-load, structural load, or workforce occupancy. If the Company later leases a small administrative office in Bermuda, it must obtain a fire-safety occupancy certificate from the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service and a building-compliance inspection from the Department of Planning before staff occupy the premises; any locally employed personnel remain subject to Bermuda occupational health and safety obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Department of Corporate and Regulatory Services (Ministry of Finance) via the Bermuda Companies Register portal, supplemented by the Office of the Tax Commissioner (Payroll Tax only) and Bermuda Customs Department (import duty only). Bermuda has no national income tax authority and issues no TIN; the statutory identity is the Bermuda Company Registration Number (BCN).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign founders incorporate through a licensed Bermuda Corporate Service Provider; the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation with a unique company registration number within 1-2 business days. No TIN/VAT ID is issued because Bermuda levies no income tax and no VAT/GST. A Payroll Tax employer account with the Office of the Tax Commissioner is triggered only upon hiring Bermuda-resident employees; a Customs importer code is required only for physical imports. For SaaS operations via Stripe and ACH, only the incorporation certificate, registered office certificate, and UBO filings are reciprocity-standard.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — offshore exempted company profits, capital gains, and dividends are exempt from all Bermudian income, corporation, and capital taxes; annual government fee is the only fiscal charge.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Domestic law: no check-the-box regime exists. US check-the-box: Bermuda corporations are on the default per se corporation list, so no US disreg-entity election is permissible. Available elections: (i) election for permit-company status under Companies Act 1981; (ii) election of financial year-end and reporting currency; (iii) election to file consolidated Economic Substance Return (Form E) across a group; (iv) under the Economic Substance Regulations 2018, an entity carrying out a relevant activity (including financing/leasing, but not pure SaaS) must elect and evidence substance. Hybrid mismatch: because Bermuda imposes no corporate income tax, hybrid mismatch outcomes do not crystallize domestically, but UK CTA 2010 Part 6A and OECD BEPS Action 2 rules may apply to UK-linked financing structures involving the Bermuda entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None — Bermuda imposes no VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax. The sole indirect fiscal levy is import customs duty under the Bermuda Customs Tariff Act 1970, which has no application to digital SaaS cross-border supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST registration threshold exists. Employers register for Payroll Tax at the first hire of a Bermuda-resident employee (combined employer-employee rate band 4.75%-8.25% of remuneration). Commercial importers require a Bermuda Customs Department registration code for duty assessment on physical goods; digital revenue is outside any indirect-tax registration trigger.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable — Bermuda has no real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing mandate, or digital stamping regime. Electronic invoicing is contractually optional. The Bermuda Customs Management System (BCMS) enables electronic import declarations solely for physical goods; no API tax-clearance gateway exists for software or SaaS invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — as a Tax_Exempt_Zone jurisdiction, Bermuda has no VAT/GST mechanism and therefore no export zero-rating or refund scheme. The Bermuda Exempted Company realizes its fiscal benefit through absolute territorial exemption of offshore income rather than exporter refunds. For UK/EU sales, the Bermuda supplier is treated as outside the UK VAT territory; UK VAT (20%) on B2C digital services is collected via UK OSS/VAT MOSS only if the company elects voluntary registration, and no input VAT refund is claimable in Bermuda because none exists.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable for pure SaaS/PropTech platform — digital services do not cross a customs border
If bundled physical hardware ever attaches: Bermuda Customs Export Declaration via BCMS
Executed SaaS subscription agreement and itemized invoice with ISIC 6201 service description
Stripe Billing payout statements and ACH inward-remittance records evidencing non-Bermuda receipts
Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Certificate for bank/counterparty KYC substantiation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback exists in Bermuda because no export zero-rating mechanism applies. The enforceable exposures are: (i) late or false Annual Economic Substance Filing (Form E) — up to BD$100,000 plus BD$10,000 per day for continuing default, and director penalties or strike-off; (ii) annual exempted-company government fee arrears attracting incremental fees and potential deregistration; (iii) a UK OSS misuse or fraudulent UK VAT credit claim attracts UK Penalty Regime (up to 100% of tax per FA 2021 Sch 16) and potential personal liability; (iv) US controlling shareholders failing Form 5471 reporting face US penalties up to US$10,000 per form per year; (v) misclassification of the Bermuda entity as a 'tax-exempt shell' in banking AML reviews triggers enhanced due diligence and potential de-risking, which is a commercial penalty equivalent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA), acting as the central bank and exchange control authority under the Bermuda Exchange Control Act 1952, the Banks and Deposit Companies Act 1999, and the Investment Business Act 2003; the UK Financial Conduct Authority retains prudential oversight relevance only for UK-linked passported activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermudian dollar (BMD) is pegged at 1:1 to the US dollar and is freely convertible for non-resident designated accounts and Exempted Companies. Bermuda maintains a two-tier exchange control regime: resident accounts require BMA permission for capital outflows, while non-resident accounts enjoy unrestricted current and capital convertibility. Profit remittance hurdles for a Bermuda Exempted Company are low: dividends require a solvency statement by the directors, compliance with the Companies Act 1981, and, where the payee is a resident account, an exchange-control final permission. No withholding tax is imposed on dividends, interest, royalties, or capital gains, but anti-money-laundering clearance and formal board authorisation are required for all outward distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirement applies to export receipts realised by a non-resident designated Bermuda Exempted Company. Export invoices may be settled in BMD, USD, or any freely convertible currency and may be retained offshore indefinitely. Where receipts are credited to a resident operating account in Bermuda, an exchange-control report must be filed with an authorised bank, and the BMA may require a declaration of source and final destination for statistical purposes. No specified conversion ratio or mandatory surrender timeline is imposed for modern SaaS/PaaS export revenue under the Exchange Control Act 1952, provided the monetary transactions exceed the BMA de minimis reporting threshold and are disclosed in the annual exchange-control return.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited (Butterfield)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operational Account and USD Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with BMD/USD settlement capability and escrow services
Corporate Current Account linked to HSBC Group global payment rails
Capital Escrow Account and treasury account for enhanced transaction flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border digital EMI viability is Medium with material legal constraints. Offshore EMI providers that have not established a branch, subsidiary, or formal BMA-licensed money service business presence in Bermuda cannot open local BMD accounts or act as a Bermuda settlement bank. EMIs lawfully passporting in the EEA/UK may service the entity on a cross-border basis for non-Bermudian receipts, but BMA-regulated banks will not rely solely on an unlicensed EMI for AML/CTF compliance. Recommended structure: engage a FCA-authorised EMI (e.g., numbered payment-institution corridor) for Stripe settlement aggregation and use Butterfield or Clarien as the ultimate BMD/USD clearing bank; obtain a BMA exemption letter where the EMI activity is treated as auxiliary to the SaaS treasury function.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence requirement exists for the corporate entity through its Bermuda registered agent and, for the beneficial owners, a personally attended identity-verification step before a notary or corresponding banker. BMA-regulated banks have adopted hybrid onboarding: the directors and ultimate beneficial owners may complete a video-interview with the Compliance Officer, but a certified physical attestation by a Bermuda attorney, a notarised passport copy, and an original Board Resolution must be forwarded through the registered agent. Full physical appearance at the bank's Bermuda premises is waived only for a Low-Risk_Standard PropTech SaaS company where the company has a local director or a pre-existing banking relationship with the group; remote opening requires enhanced due diligence on the source of SaaS receipts, the software contract counterparties, and the UBO structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of sufficient economic substance and operational footprint in Bermuda
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda registered office certificate; lease or service agreement for local premises; payroll records for resident directors/employees; minutes of board meetings held in Bermuda; group chart demonstrating decision-making management; audited financial statements and BMA economic substance return.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration of SaaS revenue from unrelated jurisdictions with no clear end-customer documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed list of customer contracts and licences; Stripe/Billing settlement reports; privacy/ISAE 3402 SOC 2 reports demonstrating data flows; transfer-pricing documentation; a payment flow diagram connecting PropTech customers to subscription billing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque source of capital for the exempted company funding contribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' source-of-wealth statement; bank statements of the contributing shareholder for the preceding 12 months; apostilled certificate of corporate formation and register of directors; signed capital contribution deed; BMA-compliant declaration on no crypto proceeds converted to fiat.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exchange-control status ambiguity and potential resident-status classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BMA-issued non-resident designation certificate; Exchange Control Act permission for the initial share issue; declaration that all beneficial owners and directors are non-resident designees; completed BMA annual exchange-control questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Named-bearer share legacy concerns or complex nominee UBO chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Registrar of Companies' current register of members; clean corporate registry search report; identification of all individuals holding >10% on a look-through basis; proof of compliance with the Economic Substance (Companies and Limited Partnerships) Act 2023 and Tax Information Exchange arrangements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be wired by SWIFT MT103 with explicit Purpose Code 'CASH FM' or 'FDI' (foreign direct investment) and the beneficiary account held at Butterfield or Clarien. The remitter must include in field 72 the unique shareholder resolution number, the exempted company's exchange-control approval reference, and the phrase 'Bermuda Exempted Company capital contribution' to satisfy BMA scrutiny. Settlement should be routed through the correspondent US clearing bank of the receiving Bermuda bank; payment must originate exclusively from a recognised regulated bank account in the shareholder's jurisdiction of tax residence. Verification requires the bank to receive a certified copy of the share allotment resolution, application for exchange-control permission from the Bermuda Ministry of Finance (where applicable), UBO identification, and a signed receipt that the payment is not a repayable loan. Hybrid capital, debt-equity swaps, or crypto-asset proceeds are accepted only after enhanced due diligence and a formal economic-substance explanation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 for single high-value vendor invoices, MT202 COV for interbank cover, and SWIFT MT700/Irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) for enterprise infrastructure or PropTech hardware procurement. Domestic operating disbursements in Bermuda use the Bermuda Automated Clearing House (ACH) for BMD-denominated payroll and landlord payments, while cross-border US subscription costs use Stripe Billing and US ACH Direct with Butterfield's US correspondent network. Every outbound payment must be uploaded with the underlying commercial invoice, a board-approved treasury execution memo, and a regular pattern validation for AML sanctions screening. No round-tripping or unstructured token disbursement is permitted; all vendor payments must clear to a named bank beneficiary with a valid LEI/BIC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/BMD FX forwards executed onshore with a BMA-licensed Bermuda bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with USD fixing for offshore settlement through Butterfield or HSBC
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between BMD-denominated operational funding and USD SaaS subscriptions
OTC vanilla FX options and collars with UK prime brokers under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
FX swaps used solely for temporary treasury matching of Stripe settlement cycles and Bermuda operational funding

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Maintenance Fee (Exempted Company Tier)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers automatic 10% late fee surcharge; continued non-payment after notice results in administrative strike-off and dissolution under the Companies Act 1981, Section 103.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Current Members / Share Capital Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default fine of up to USD 500 per month; repeated default is a continuing offence and is an additional ground for administrative strike-off after three months of non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration (if relevant activity applies, including IP/digital commerce activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Tax Commissioner, Economic Substance Unit, Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the applicable financial year; commonly aligned with the annual return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence carrying a fine up to USD 10,000; continued default may trigger up to 2 years imprisonment or further daily penalties and referral to the Ministry of Finance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required for a Bermuda Exempted Company unless it qualifies as a 'small company' under the Companies Act (Audit Exemption) Regulations; a company qualifies if it has 25 or fewer members and does not exceed two of: annual gross revenue USD 5,000,000, total assets USD 5,000,000, or average employment of 25 persons. Shareholder unanimous approval is required for any exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (Bermuda harmonised) or US GAAP, both accepted by the Registrar of Companies; preparation and content governed by the Companies Act 1981 and applicable accounting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The exempted company must file an annual beneficial ownership confirmation with the Registrar of Companies through the integrated registry; confirmation is due within 15 days after the anniversary of incorporation. Any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be recorded in the Register of Members and the Beneficial Ownership Register within 14 days of the change. Bearer shares are prohibited or fully immobilised, and any transfer must trigger immediate register update and annual reconfirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 3,500 per year for a Bermuda registered agent and registered office provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 25,000 for a PropTech (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 531390) holding entity with standard consolidated transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for Bermuda Exempted Companies outside the scope of the Bermuda corporate income tax regime; 15% only for constituent entities of multinational groups with consolidated global revenue exceeding EUR 750m under the Bermuda Corporate Income Tax Act 2023, effective for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential income tax deductions exist in Bermuda. Exempted companies enjoy tax neutrality on offshore income, capital gains, dividends, interest and royalties. Applicable ancillary charges such as Bermuda Payroll Tax, Social Insurance Contributions and annual government fees are sector-specific and are not income-tax reliefs. For in-scope MNE groups, a qualified domestic minimum top-up tax applies within the 15% Bermuda CIT framework, with no zero-rate incentive.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Economic Substance Declaration (ES Declaration) filed through the Registrar of Companies E-Filing system (www.registry.gov.bm) under the Economic Substance Regulations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the entity's financial year. A common default is a 31 December year-end with a filing deadline of 30 June; the declaration must be filed before the Registrar's annual closure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Bermuda Exempted Company, registration number, registered office address and local registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name on the Certificate of Incorporation; the registered office must be in Bermuda and a licensed local registered agent must be named.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting period start and end dates for the annual declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same fiscal period as the ultimate parent when consolidated, provided the period does not exceed 12 months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classification of the entity's income-generating activity under the Economic Substance Regulations: Banking, Insurance, Fund Management, Financing & Leasing, Headquarters, Shipping, Holding, Distribution & Service, or Intellectual Property. A PropTech software platform is likely to be treated as a Distribution & Service or Intellectual Property business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review intercompany contracts, licence agreements and group charts. The activity must be determined on a standalone basis even where the ultimate parent is non-Bermudian.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed disclosure of physical presence: number of full-time employees in Bermuda, operating expenditure, board meeting frequency and location, management control, and core income-generating activities performed in Bermuda.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A remote-only setup without any Bermuda employees or premises will fail the economic substance test. Non-resident beneficial owners must not cause the entity to be managed and controlled wholly outside Bermuda.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of the Economic Substance Declaration attracts an automatic civil penalty of BMD 25,000; continued default may result in BMD 50,000 plus daily penalties up to BMD 500 per day. Knowingly providing false information is punishable by fines up to BMD 100,000 and imprisonment of the responsible officers for up to 5 years. The Registrar may strike the company off the register or apply to the Minister for dissolution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda Corporate Income Tax Return (CITR) filed through the Bermuda Tax Administration's online portal by in-scope multinational group constituent entities under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023. Out-of-scope Exempted Companies have no CIT filing obligation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The CIT return is due within 12 months after the fiscal year-end. Estimated tax instalments are payable quarterly during the year, with the final balance due upon filing the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Consolidated group name, ultimate parent entity identifier and jurisdiction, and consolidated global revenue used to determine whether the EUR 750m threshold is exceeded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Bermuda Exempted Company must report an accurate group structure even if all shareholders and ultimate decision-makers are outside Bermuda.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Bermuda taxable income under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023, applying arm's length transfer pricing to related-party transactions and adjusting GAAP accounts in accordance with statutory rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany pricing must be supported by contemporaneous documentation in Bermuda even where the counterparties are non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT due at 15% after crediting any qualified domestic minimum top-up tax from other group entities and applying allowable carryforward losses, limited to the 5-year statutory loss period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident group members may not transfer operating losses to the Bermuda entity unless the loss has been actually recognised within the Bermuda taxable unit under the CIT Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax due per month, capped at 25%; late payment interest at 3% above the Bermuda central bank discount rate; intentional understatement is subject to a penalty up to 100% of the tax due. Directors and senior officers may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid withholding and CIT where they participate in default.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Bermuda imposes no statutory withholding tax on dividend distributions made by a Bermuda Exempted Company to any shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Bermuda does not maintain comprehensive double taxation agreements and imposes no domestic dividend withholding tax, so no treaty relief application is required for dividends paid out of Bermuda. Where a foreign parent jurisdiction requires proof of Bermuda tax status, the Exempted Company may obtain a Certificate of Tax Residency from the Office of the Tax Commissioner by filing the prescribed application with the certificate of incorporation and a written declaration of non-taxability. The certificate is typically issued within 5–10 business days and merely certifies the entity's residence and exempt status under Bermuda law.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory Bermuda withholding tax on interest, royalties, management fees and similar cross-border payments. No treaty rate applies. Payments by a Bermuda Exempted Company to non-resident licensors or lenders are outside Bermuda income tax and are not subject to any local notional tax deduction. Recipients may, however, be exposed to anti-hybrid, CFC or transfer-pricing adjustments in their own jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory transfer-pricing documentation threshold applies to out-of-scope Bermuda Exempted Companies. For in-scope MNE groups subject to the Bermuda Corporate Income Tax Act 2023, contemporaneous documentation is required where the group has worldwide revenue of at least EUR 750m (approximately BMD 750m) and Bermuda connected-party transactions exceed BMD 1m in a fiscal year. The threshold is denominated in BMD, with 1 BMD pegged to 1 USD.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are fully applicable to every Bermuda Exempted Company. A PropTech SaaS entity deriving revenue from software licences, cloud solutions or real-estate data services will typically be classified as an Intellectual Property Business or a Distribution & Service Business. The entity must demonstrate in each financial year: (i) management and control exercised in Bermuda; (ii) a physical office in Bermuda; (iii) an adequate and qualified employee headcount in Bermuda; and (iv) core income-generating activities performed in Bermuda. Pure holding and shareholder activities remain subject to a lighter substance test, but no exemption is available for an active operating digital platform.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic Substance Evasion / False ESR Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Bermuda Exempted Company as a tax-exempt shell while all management, staffing and commercial activity remain in a foreign substantive jurisdiction; filing an Economic Substance Declaration falsely claiming Bermuda employees, premises, board meetings and core income-generating activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Regulations, the first default is subject to a civil penalty of BMD 25,000; continued default attracts BMD 50,000 plus daily penalties up to BMD 500 per day. Knowingly filing a false declaration is punishable by a fine up to BMD 100,000 and imprisonment of the responsible officers for up to 5 years. The Registrar may strike off the company, arrange its dissolution through the Minister, and exchange information with foreign tax authorities pursuant to Bermuda's Tax Information Exchange Agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors and beneficial owners personally liable for unpaid penalties and third-party losses. Directors face disqualification, travel bans, asset freezes and imprisonment up to 5 years for knowingly certifying false economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Aggressive Cross-Border Tax Evasion / Tax Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Bermuda Exempted Company to artificially strip profits out of high-tax jurisdictions through royalty, interest or service-fee arrangements that lack commercial reasoning, personnel or operational capacity; claiming the 0% tax regime while directing uncontrolled profits from a European PropertyTech SaaS market to Bermuda without value creation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The foreign jurisdiction may apply its general anti-avoidance rules, CFC rules, transfer-pricing adjustments and anti-hybrid rules, recharacterising payments, denying deductions and imposing penalties up to 100% of the tax due plus interest. If the group is within the Bermuda CIT threshold, Bermuda will impose 15% CIT on the recharacterised Bermuda income and can penalise false filings. Foreign asset-freeze orders and criminal prosecution may follow under bilateral mutual legal assistance arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally liable for civil restitution, denial of travel, asset seizure and imprisonment under money-laundering statutes if they knowingly sign false transfer-pricing documentation or distribute artificially structured profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and Shell Company Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining no physical presence, no independent Bermuda employees, no board minutes, no transparent bank account records, and receiving SaaS revenues through third-party payment processors while immediately repatriating funds as tax-free dividends to foreign shareholders for no demonstrable commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Bermuda's Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering) Regulations and Financial Sanctions Enforcement Unit powers, failure to conduct due diligence or to maintain AML/CFT governance attracts penalties up to BMD 100,000 and criminal fines. The Registrar may refuse annual certification and the Supreme Court may order administrative dissolution or a prohibition order against the directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and beneficial owners are personally exposed to AML enforcement. Banks may terminate accounts, file suspicious activity reports, freeze assets and trigger travel alerts. Individuals may be prosecuted for money-laundering and, upon conviction, sentenced to imprisonment without the protection of the corporate form.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Filing and Payment Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Bermuda Exempted Company is part of a multinational group with consolidated global revenue exceeding EUR 750m, but the directors fail to register with the Bermuda Tax Administration, file the annual CIT return, or pay quarterly instalments of the 15% Bermuda corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing attracts 5% of the tax due for each month, up to a maximum of 25%; late payment interest is charged at 3% above the Bermuda central bank discount rate. The Tax Commissioner may issue an estimated assessment, seize assets, and register a statutory charge. Knowingly omitting Bermuda taxable income may expose the company to a penalty of up to 100% of the tax due and administrative fines up to BMD 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid employee withholdings and CIT where they knowingly participate in non-payment. Courts may grant personal civil restitution, travel bans and asset seizures after proving that the director directed or ignored unlawful filing failures. Imprisonment of up to 5 years applies for fraudulent evasion or knowingly false returns.
